page: Microsoft Azure FX4ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the FXmsv2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and integer operations. The instance is provisioned with 84.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 21.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core (2353.0) and text processing (2822.0), alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression (34.8 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.49 GB/sec). However, multi-core performance is constrained by the 2-core physical hardware limit, resulting in weak ratings for stress-ng multi-core (4441.77) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.65 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth also shows a tradeoff, with strong cached read speeds of 348.09 GB/sec but weak uncached large-block read (36.48 GB/sec) and write (25.67 GB/sec) performance.

Given its high memory density relative to its compute footprint, the FX4ms_v2 is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 6.29 million SET operations per second in benchmarks), and single-threaded text or data processing tasks. The dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores provide strong single-thread execution, but the low physical core count makes it less efficient for highly parallelized workloads, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
